profile.reading: LightEdge Austin I sits in Travis County, Texas, though LightEdge own site publishes two distinct Austin addresses, 2916 Montopolis Drive and 7000-B Burleson Road, with an unresolved discrepancy between LightEdge own pages over the Burleson Road building suite number and zip code, and no source reviewed this session could confirm which specific address corresponds to this record Austin I designation as opposed to the separate Austin II record elsewhere in this dataset. Per LightEdge own combined specification sheet for the Austin market, the facility or facilities together provide 2.5 megawatts of critical IT load and 8.25 megawatts of generator capacity with an isolated 2N UPS configuration, across 58,471 total square feet including 40,960 square feet of white space. The facility carries a broad compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS, with nine on-net carriers including AT&T, Cogent, Lumen, Zayo, and Spectrum. LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. LightEdge announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm, in September 2021, and underwent a CEO transition from longtime leader Jim Masterson to Rob Carter effective January 1, 2025. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets plus a location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named for this facility, and no year-built or tier-rating figure is disclosed for the Austin market on LightEdge own site. Austin has grown rapidly as a Texas technology hub over the past decade, drawing both large hyperscale campuses from other operators and mid-market colocation demand of the kind LightEdge compliance-focused business model typically serves, consistent with the company decision to maintain two separate buildings in that specific metro.

LightEdge Austin I sits at an address in Travis County but publishes no power capacity figure, making its size unknown to this registry. The operator's own specification page references critical IT capacity and total square footage without disclosing exact numbers, available only through a downloadable spec sheet not accessed in this research pass. Without published watts, this campus cannot be ranked by power among the 18 facilities in Texas that do disclose figures.

The facility exists as one of 133 mapped data center locations in Texas, a state with 468 megawatts of published IT capacity across disclosed sites. LightEdge operates a second Austin building nearby, but only this address is recorded here. No certifications, colocation terms, or grid connection details are published.

This campus cannot be assessed for its relevance to AI scaling without power figures. Whether it hosts training infrastructure, inference clusters, or serves other workloads remains unknown. To evaluate its role in the state's compute landscape, published specifications on capacity would be required.
